title: refactor(ci): consolidate workflows, optimize cache & parallelism
author: Elena Park
description: Motivation: our repo accumulated many siloed GitHub Actions workflows over the last 18 months, leading to duplicated steps, long queue times, and inconsistent caching strategy across packages. This PR consolidates the lint/test/release workflows into a smaller set of composable jobs, standardizes cache keys, and introduces controlled parallelism for test matrices to reduce wall-time without degrading runner utilization. Highlights: - Combine node/matrix/linters into shared workflow templates (actions/workflow-templates/) - Standardize cache keys: use repo+hash of lockfile + job-specific suffix to avoid stale cache misses - Introduce a single reusable job for build/test that accepts strategy/parallelism params - Reduce default matrix parallelism from 8 -> 4 on public runners, add knob for repo-owners to increase on dedicated runners - Add gating job for release automation to run only on release branches and when changelog label is present - Update action versions to pinned stable releases (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/cache@v4) - Improve logging and step-level timing metrics to surface slow tasks Checklist: - [x] Move shared steps to actions/.github/workflows/templates - [x] Update package-level workflows to call reusable jobs - [x] Validate cache hits on CI (measurement included in CI checks) - [x] Run integration smoke tests on dedicated runners - [x] Update docs/CONTRIBUTING.md with new dev workflow Developer notes / migration: - Maintainers: no immediate action required unless you manage a package that relies on >8 matrix parallelism. See README at .github/workflows/README.md for override knobs. - Releases: release workflow now requires the label "release" on PRs targeting release/* branches, see release notes below. Testing performed: - Ran the full CI matrix across redwood, redwood-sdk-python, and redwood-quickstarts using dedicated runners. - Observed ~28% median wall-time reduction on lint+test jobs with same total runner-minutes due to improved cache reuse and reduced cold-starts. - Measured cache hit ratio improvement from 63% -> 87% after key normalization. Related: ENG-2048 (ci cost reductions), ENG-2099 (release automation hygiene).

release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows (lint/test/release) into reusable templates; improved cache key strategy (higher cache hit rate); reduced default matrix parallelism to 4; pinned GitHub Actions to stable v4 releases; added docs for maintainers to override parallelism on dedicated runners.
notes_for_oncall: No rollbacks required. If you observe higher queue times on public runners after merge, check the per-repo override knobs in .github/workflows/README.md and the 'parallelism' input for reusable jobs. The release workflow is gated by the 'release' label to avoid accidental runs.
